summary: A funnel that shows how many people reach each stage of a flow, like signup to paid, with the stage that loses the largest share marked. Under the funnel sits a short note, written by your agent, explaining what the numbers mean. A switch moves between segments such as all users, teams and solo users.
use: When you want to show conversion through a signup, onboarding or checkout flow.
When an agent analyses the funnel and its finding should sit right under the chart.
When the same stages need comparing across a few user segments.
features: One horizontal bar per entry in `stages`, its width relative to the first stage, with the count on or beside the bar.
Each row ends with its drop from the stage before as a percentage, and the first row reads 100%.
The stage with the largest drop compared with the one before is marked automatically.
Hovering a bar shows its share of the first stage, ended by `shareLabel`, or `startLabel` on the first stage.
With more than one entry in `views`, a segment switch redraws the bars top to bottom and swaps in that view's `insight` text.
a11y: The segment switch is a role="group" labelled "Segment", and its buttons use aria-pressed.
Each bar's share tooltip has role="tooltip".

faq.q: Does the component write the insight text?
faq.a: No. You pass it as `insight` on each view, for example a summary your agent produced. The component only picks out and marks the biggest drop.

faq.q: How is the biggest drop chosen?
faq.a: It is the stage whose count is the smallest fraction of the stage before it, which is not always the largest absolute loss.

faq.q: How do I word the hover tip for my data?
faq.a: Set `shareLabel`, like "of signups", to read "51.8% of signups", and `startLabel` for the first stage's tip.

faq.q: Can I show a single funnel without the switch?
faq.a: Yes. Pass one entry in `views`. The switch only appears when there is more than one, and the note only shows if a view has an `insight`.
